reports.title: Sophia Ayuk: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: A full review of the Trust's VTE policy
promises.summary: Review VTE policy to improve risk assessment compliance

promises.quote: A VTE Screening and Assessment Clinical Alert was disseminated across the Trust
promises.summary: Disseminate clinical alert on VTE screening

promises.quote: Changes were made to the new doctors' induction and junior doctors handbook to include information on VTE assessments
promises.summary: Update induction and handbook with VTE assessment guidance

promises.quote: Anti-psychotic medication has been added as a consideration on the Trust's VTE assessment tool
promises.summary: Add anti-psychotic consideration to VTE assessment tool

promises.quote: The Trust's monthly two day physical health training programme now includes a session on VTE risk
promises.summary: Include VTE risk session in monthly training programme

promises.quote: A yellow card warning was raised with the manufacturers of the anti-psychotic, Zaponex through the Medicines Health Regulations Authority (MHRA) to alert to two patients who have both passed away from pulmonary embolism whilst on Zaponex
promises.summary: Issue yellow card warning to manufacturers about Zaponex risks

concerns.quote: At no time during the two periods of Ms [name redacted] inpatient care was she assessed for venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk in contravention of trust policy.
Instructions given to monitor and record Ms [name redacted] food and fluid intake were not adequately followed.
concerns.hazard: inadequate monitoring of food and fluid intake

reports.title: Nimo Osman: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: Following the discovery of Ms [name redacted] collapse on Rosebank Ward on 21 April 2022, it took staff a significant number of minutes to recognise that instead of just lying on the floor, Ms Osman was actually unrousable. A few minutes later a nurse arrived on the scene, who decided to summon the duty senior nurse (DSN) by radio, rather than activating the alarm system, which would have summoned the rapid response team sooner. The DSN contacted the duty doctor to inform them that there was a medical emergency
Staff should consider whether patients' behaviour might be due to being physically unwell and not assume that this is due to their mental health condition.
concerns.hazard: assumption of mental cause over physical cause

concerns.quote: As per Physical Healthcare Policy, v.14.1, Feb 2021, 7.6, all patients should have a VTE risk assessment form completed and a VTE assessment on admission to the in-patient unit.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that patients were not receiving the required venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk assessment during inpatient care. The later report notes that the VTE assessment policy has not been fully embedded, leaving the same hazard unresolved.

links.later_quote: As per Physical Healthcare Policy, v.14.1, Feb 2021, 7.6, all patients should have a VTE risk assessment form completed and a VTE assessment on admission to the in-patient unit.

followups.summary: The Trust's policy and procedure page indicates that policies are added when approved, but no specific mention of a VTE screening alert is provided. The document lists various policies but does not reference the promised clinical alert.
